newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Iran's Velayati urges peace talks in Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Velayati urges peace talks in Afghanistan.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said on Wednesday that the crisis in Afghanistan could not be resolved by force and called on all the factions to negotiate a peaceful settlement.
"We believe that (the) Afghanistan problem doesn't have a military solution," Velayati said after discussing the fighting in Afghanistan with Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev.
"All factions should sit down together, talk together to reach a peaceful settlement in Afghanistan," he told reporters.

Velayati is on a lightning tour of the former Soviet republics of Central Asia to discuss events in Afghanistan, where government forces are battling the radical Islamic Taleban militia who drove them out of the capital late last month.
Neighbouring Pakistan offered on Tuesday to mediate between the warring factions.

But this offer is unlikely to suit the Iranians, whose media have accused Pakistan, the United States and Saudi Arabia of provoking the situation inside the mountainous country torn apart by years of bloody civil war.

"The intervention of other countries in the internal affairs of Afghanistan is the main original problem and the main victims in this process are the people of Afghanistan," said Velayati, who did not name any of the states.
"We don't want to intervene in the internal affairs of Afghanistan or any other countries," he said.
Iran recognises the ousted government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani, driven out of the Afghan capital last month.
Earlier on Wednesday, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported that all but one of Iran's diplomats had been withdrawn from Kabul.
Velayati is scheduled to travel to the Central Asian republic of Tajikistan on Wednesday and afterwards to Uzbekistan. Both countries, along with Turkmenistan, border Afghanistan.

Russia and all the Central Asian republics except Turkmenistan said after a meeting in Almaty earlier this month that they would take unspecified measures to prevent the Afghan war from spilling over into their territories.
But they said they would not intervene in the conflict.
Iran is keen to strengthen its influence in the oil-rich Central Asian region, particularly in the sphere of oil and gas export routes out of the landlocked area.
